verdict: Netflix grew revenue 16% to $11.1B as every region expanded, and with costs growing far more slowly than sales, its operating margin hit 34% and net income jumped 46% to $3.1B.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $4.88 a year ago (both as reported, before the 10-for-1 stock split)

segments.name: United States & Canada
segments.note: The biggest and richest market — subscription streaming, plus the fast-growing ads business.

segments.name: Europe, Middle East & Africa
segments.note: The second-largest region — up 18% as reported.

segments.name: Latin America
segments.note: Cheaper plans are pulling in new households — up 9% as reported.

segments.name: Asia-Pacific
segments.note: Mobile-first plans in price-sensitive markets — the fastest-growing region, up 24%.

opex.name: Technology & development
opex.note: The streaming platform, apps, recommendation systems and the new in-house ad-tech stack.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Advertising Netflix itself and winning subscribers.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company: legal, finance and offices.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $183M on Netflix's debt, partly offset by $40M of interest and other income — a net -$143M below operating profit.
footerNote: Regional revenues are from Netflix's Q2 2025 10-Q. Figures are rounded to whole $M; the tax line is shown as $507M ($506M as reported) so the chart ties exactly to the reported $3,125M of net income.

takeaways.title: The margin keeps expanding
takeaways.text: Operating income rose 45% YoY to $3.8B — revenue grew 16% while the cost of revenues grew just 3%, so the operating margin widened from 27% a year ago to 34%.

takeaways.title: Every region grew
takeaways.text: Asia-Pacific led at +24%, EMEA rose 18%, the U.S. & Canada 15% and Latin America 9% — growth no longer depends on any single market.

takeaways.title: Cash-flow guidance raised
takeaways.text: Netflix raised its full-year 2025 free-cash-flow forecast to $8–8.5B and guided to 17% revenue growth in Q3 — price rises and the young ads business are doing the work.
